crumbs.name: Knowledge Based Professions and their Future

children.name: Drafting Proposal Responses
children.blurb: Drafting proposal responses in finance covers the assembly of written answers to requests for proposals, due diligence questionnaires, and client or counterparty information requests.

children.name: Agent Negotiation in Over-the-Counter Markets
children.blurb: Agent negotiation in over the counter markets covers software agents that represent buyers, sellers, dealers, or clients in bilateral and voice or chat based trading of instruments not listed on exchanges, such as swaps, bonds, FX forwards, and structured notes.

children.name: Investment Committee Memos
children.blurb: Investment committee memos are the formal documents that present a proposed investment to the committee that approves, rejects, or conditions it.

children.name: Keeping Comparable Company Sets Current
children.blurb: Keeping comparable company sets current means maintaining a peer group used for valuation, relative performance, and sector benchmarking as the underlying companies change.

children.name: Automating Trade Settlement
children.blurb: Automating trade settlement covers the post-trade steps that turn an executed trade into a final transfer of cash and securities, including trade enrichment, matching, confirmation, clearing, settlement instruction generation, reconciliation, and fails management.

sections.body: Agent workflows in finance are software systems that carry out multi-step tasks across documents, messages, and market data, with humans setting policy and reviewing exceptions. In practice, AI is drafting responses to requests for proposals, proposing and countering terms in over-the-counter negotiations, assembling investment committee memos from filings and models, refreshing comparable company sets, and preparing settlement instructions. These are not autonomous traders or advisors. They are workflow agents that read, summarize, extract, draft, route, and reconcile. The work is narrow and often supervised. The value comes from speed and consistency on repetitive, document-heavy steps.
sections.heading: What this covers

sections.body: Some parts are more mature than others. Document drafting and memo assembly are widely assisted by language models, but they still need source checks and human sign-off. Negotiation agents can generate and evaluate offers in structured settings, yet they struggle with incomplete information, strategic ambiguity, and counterparties who change terms. Comparable company updates are partly automated through data feeds and filing monitors, though taxonomy and timing issues remain. Settlement automation is well established in parts of post-trade processing, but exceptions, fails, and cross-border rules keep humans in the loop. Honest limits include hallucination, stale data, audit trails, and the difficulty of proving that an agent followed a mandate.
sections.heading: Where the work stands

sections.body: The pages here follow a deal and trade lifecycle. Drafting Proposal Responses covers the front end, where agents assemble client-ready answers from prior bids and internal material. Agent Negotiation in Over-the-Counter Markets looks at the middle, where agents propose, evaluate, and log bilateral terms. Investment Committee Memos shows how agents turn diligence, models, and market context into a reviewable decision document. Keeping Comparable Company Sets Current addresses the ongoing data hygiene that supports valuation and benchmarking, and the site's 357 merger and acquisition filings are one example of the source material that must be monitored. Automating Trade Settlement closes the loop on post-trade instructions, confirmations, and exceptions, so a reader can move from one page to the next to see where agents assist, where they only draft, and where a human still owns the decision.
